cohort.note: A sweep of all 676 bills this corpus cites compared each citation against the real title of the bill it names. 262 citations across 17 bills point at a real but UNRELATED bill. The correct number is demonstrably known to the corpus -- for most of these acts it cites BOTH a right and a wrong number -- which is what makes them repairable rather than simply wrong.

the_finding_that_shaped_every_verdict.headline: FOR A VOTE CLAIM THE CORRECT INSTRUMENT IS ALMOST NEVER THE BILL THAT CARRIES THE ACT'S NAME.
the_finding_that_shaped_every_verdict.detail: A Massachusetts landmark act is filed under one number, amended, REPRINTED under another, sent across, and finally enacted as a conference report under a number nobody outside the building would recognise -- and the bill the public knows may never be voted on at all.

enacted_vehicles.ROE Act: 191/H5179 "An Act providing for access to reproductive health services", section 40 of the FY21 budget, Chapter 263 of the Acts of 2020. ITS OWN BILL, H.3320 of the 191st, DIED -- "No further action taken", 1/5/2021 -- and never reached a floor vote. House 107-46 on the veto override (#374), 107-50 on re-enactment (#317); Senate 32-8 (#372).
enacted_vehicles.Police reform: 191/S2963, Chapter 253 of 2020 (S.2800 -> S.2820 -> S.2963). House 91-67 on enactment (#285), 107-51 on re-enactment (#326); Senate 28-12 on the conference report (#300).
enacted_vehicles.Affordable Homes Act: 193/H4977, Chapter 150 of 2024 -- the one act here whose familiar number IS the enacted vehicle. House 128-24 (#199); Senate 37-2 (#249).

the_finding_that_shaped_every_verdict.consequence: A sponsorship claim is tested against the FILED bill's cosponsor list, a vote claim against the ENACTED vehicle's roll call. They are different documents answering different questions. A first pass that checked sponsorship first "confirmed" eight rows saying "voted for the ROE Act" by finding the member on H.3320's cosponsor list -- not the same fact, and the prose would still have asserted a vote nobody had checked.

the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.what_1899_recorded: MA roll-call PDFs "can prove a NAY, never a YEA": pdftotext -layout recovered 14/14 nays but only 39 of 144 yeas on S.9, so most of this cohort could only have been blanked -- over-retiring claims that are probably TRUE.
the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.the_cause: Not the PDF. The roll call is a four-column grid whose THIRD COLUMN sits at a slightly different vertical offset, so -layout assigns every second name of that column to the gap line BETWEEN grid rows, orphaned from its marker.
the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.the_fix: Xpdf pdftotext has a `-table` mode that groups words into grid CELLS by position rather than by raster line. Then TOKENISE each cell line on runs of 2+ spaces instead of regexing it: a boundary regex drops "--Jones--", which does not begin with a letter, and swallows the next cell after "Farley-Bouvier", which is only two spaces from the next marker.
the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.senate_is_a_different_document: Senate roll calls are journal-style: a two-column list of FULL names under YEAS./NAYS. headings, each section ending in its own declared count ("Spilka, Karen E. - 28.").
the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.A_TOTALS_CHECK_IS_NOT_ENOUGH_ON_ITS_OWN: A name-shaped regex over the flattened Senate text split "Creem, Cynthia Stone" and "Lovely, Joan B." into "Creem, Cynthia" and "Stone Lovely, Joan B.". That error LOSES NO NAME AND GAINS NONE, so 40 parsed still equalled 40 declared while two senators carried the wrong surname. A count that matches does not mean the boundaries are right.
the_blocker_migration_1899_left_and_the_.verification: All ten roll calls used here parse EXACTLY, checked twice: against the PDF's own declared totals AND against the totals the bill history states independently.

the_distinctiveness_line.the_converse_still_holds: Dissent from a lopsided majority IS distinctive however lopsided the vote -- 11 rows repaired on that basis.

what_three_earlier_passes_would_have_bla: A PROFILE'S COURT LIST COVERS ONE CHAMBER ONLY. 18 of these 96 members have TWO profile pages because they moved between the branches. Reading only the chamber they sit in now declared Fernandes, Driscoll and Howard "not in the legislature" for votes they had cast as Representatives. Tenure is the UNION of both profiles.

"RIGHT NUMBER, WRONG COURT" STRUCK AGAIN, exactly as H.4264 did in 1899. H.1795 of the 193rd IS the jail and prison construction moratorium; H.1304 of the 193rd IS "An Act enabling local options for tenant protections". Only the 194th versions are unrelated. Checking the cited court alone would have blanked Tyler and Lewis, who are on them.

AN ACT IS REFILED EVERY GENERAL COURT. The Safe Communities Act exists in all of 190/H3269, 190/S1305, 191/H3573, 191/S1401, 192/H2418, 192/S1579, 193/H2288, 193/S1510, 194/H2580, 194/S1681. Michlewitz is on the 190th filing and on none of the later ones; a 193rd+194th-only check would have blanked a true claim. The search parse that hid it: malegislature renders TWO links per result, the bill number then the title, and a parser requiring the link text to start with "An Act" silently returned a fraction of the set -- which reads exactly like "this act was only ever filed once".

"OPPOSED" IS NOT ALWAYS A NO. Daniel J. Hunt was flagged as having voted the opposite of his row because its prose says he "has OPPOSED RESTRICTIONS on abortion access" -- the opposite sense, the same trap as DiDomenico's "default-to-openness" in migration 1899.

the_ladder_scope_blanks.finding: SEASON 2 DID NOT REWORD THE VOTING-RIGHTS LADDER, IT REPLACED IT. Season 1 ran "automatically register all eligible citizens to vote and allow online voting" / "expand early voting periods and make mail-in voting available to all" -- the subject of the VOTES Act. Season 2 is a pure VOTER-ID scale: rung 1 is "Require no identification to vote, verifying voters by signature", rung 4 is "Require photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot". A verified vote on the VOTES Act locates nobody on that ladder.
the_ladder_scope_blanks.disposition: Blanked with the verified vote written into the blank -- 12 Yeas and the Nays of Tarr and O'Connor. The Carson call of migration 1896; a fifth member of the ladder-scope register.
